What I see

  • Centering: the blue border looks about even left to right.
  • Color: strong blue, red and yellow, with no visible fading.
  • Corners: top-left and bottom-left look sharp. Top-right and bottom-right look slightly soft.
  • Edges: tiny white chips along the right border and the bottom edge.
  • Surface: a few small white print specks. Faint hairlines may be scratches on the holder, not the card.
  • Back: puzzle-piece back, clean and in great shape.
  • No creases, stains or writing visible.

Section 03

Estimated Grade

PSA 6–8
Most likely a 7. An 8 needs the corners and edges to hold up out of the holder. A 9 or higher is unlikely.

Pushes up

  • Even front centering and strong color
  • Clean-looking surface, no creases
  • Back in great shape

Pulls down

  • Soft right-hand corners
  • Tiny edge chips

A dealer with the card out of the holder under bright light can narrow this.

Section 05

Grading Costs

PSA tierFeeMax declared valueTurnaround
Standard (new, Sep 2026)$59.99$1,000 insuranceNot found
Regular~$80$2,499~25 business days
Express~$150$4,999~15 business days
  • Fees come from May 2026 guides plus a September 2026 news item. Confirm current prices with PSA or the dealer.
  • The cheaper Value tiers were paused during PSA’s backlog, so low-fee options may not be open.
  • At PSA 7 or 8 this card is worth more than the Regular tier’s declared-value cap. Tiers above Express exist, and I did not find their prices.
  • Declare the card’s real value. PSA can add an upcharge after grading if it lands above the tier you chose.
  • Shipping, insurance and any membership fee are extra.
  • Sources say SGC and CGC charge less and return faster, while PSA usually brings the strongest resale premium on vintage Star Wars.

Break-even: at PSA 6 the card is worth about $700 more than the ungraded average. Even at PSA 4 ($357) it clears a $150 fee.

Section 06

Authenticity and Versions

  • The blue border marks Series 1. These are different cards with their own, much lower prices: the Wonder Bread #1 (PSA 9 about $645) and the sticker #1 (PSA 10 $57,600).
  • An O-Pee-Chee (Canadian) printing of the set exists. Ask the dealer to confirm yours is the Topps US printing.
  • PSA authenticates as part of grading. A dealer can also compare the print, stock and back against known copies.

Section 07

Questions for Dealers

  • Based on the corners and edges, what grade range do you expect?
  • Should the card come out of the screw-down holder first, and who removes it safely?
  • PSA, SGC or CGC for this card, and how much does the resale price differ?
  • Which PSA tier and declared value would you use?
  • Do you submit cards for customers? What do you charge, and how long does it take?
  • Who covers insurance and shipping during submission?
  • What would you pay for it ungraded today, and on consignment after grading?
  • Can you confirm it is the Topps US printing and not an O-Pee-Chee?
